_readme: The fixed set of local tracks `mock_soundcloud.py` serves. Deterministic:
explicit ids, explicit order, no globbing and no 'whatever sorts first'.
WHY THESE FIVE, out of the ~371 audio files under ~/Music:
* They are the only files on disk that have BOTH real bytes AND
authoritative ground-truth BPM/key. ~/Music/SoundCloud holds 320 real
downloads, but 0 of them carry a BPM or key tag, and Serato's own
database (_Serato_/database V2, 215 rows / 202 with a BPM) has almost
no overlap with that folder. Of the Serato rows that do resolve, most
point into iCloud Drive at dataless placeholders — st_blocks == 0, and
reads fail with EPERM even though os.path.exists() says yes.
* Every BPM below was cross-checked against the audio by DFT tempogram
* All five are 320 kbps CBR MP3, 44.1 kHz stereo — the container
AVFoundation is least likely to surprise us on, and within MixEngine's
'stereo or mono only' limit.
* They are Serato's royalty-free Starter Pack demo content, so a fixture
server can serve them without serving someone's copyrighted rip.
ORDER IS DELIBERATE. `DemoSeed.apply()` makes tracks[0] the current track
and the whole array the queue, so tracks[0] -> tracks[1] is the pair the
DJ engine will try to mix first. That slot goes to the 120.00 -> 122.00
pair, which is 2.00 BPM apart AND harmonically adjacent (Am = 8A ->
Em = 9A, neighbours on the Camelot wheel) — a mix that should come out
clean, so anything ugly is the engine and not the material.
COVERAGE: clean blend (7002->7003), degenerate identical-BPM blend
(7004->7005), real breakdowns (7002 has three, one of them 30 s), long
quiet DJ intro (7003, 34 s), and a genuine hard stop (7004 — last audible
sample 0.168 s before EOF, no fade, no trailing silence).
CAVEAT when changing what a given id serves (e.g. adding --trim): the
decoded .caf cache in the app is keyed on `track-<id>-<preset>`, NOT on
the URL or the bytes. Re-running with the same ids will replay the stale
decode. Reinstall the app, or use Settings > clear the mix cache.

tracks.path: ~/Music/_Serato_/Imported/Serato Demo Tracks/02 - House Track Serato House Starter Pack.mp3
tracks.title: House Track 02
tracks.note: Structure reference. Three distinct breakdowns (24-30 s, 96-110 s, and a 30-second one at 176-206 s) and the longest runtime in the set, so a long crossfade has room. Smooth 3 s fade outro.

tracks.path: ~/Music/_Serato_/Imported/Serato Demo Tracks/03 - House Track Serato House Starter Pack.mp3
tracks.title: House Track 03
tracks.note: Blend partner for 7002: 2.00 BPM apart and one step round the Camelot wheel. 34 s quiet DJ intro to mix into. Ends nastily — full level to 224 s, collapsed by 228.4 s, then 7.7 s of true digital silence to EOF.

tracks.path: ~/Music/_Serato_/Imported/Serato Demo Tracks/01 - House Track Serato House Starter Pack.mp3
tracks.title: House Track 01
tracks.note: 14 s full breakdown at 62-76 s (-25 dB against a -7 dB body) and a second at 232-240 s. Fades out with 4.0 s of trailing digital silence — catches outro detection that trusts container duration.

tracks.path: ~/Music/_Serato_/Imported/Serato Demo Tracks/04 - Hip Hop Track Serato Hip Hop Starter Pack.mp3
tracks.title: Hip Hop Track 04
tracks.note: The hard stop. Last audible sample at 219.313 s of 219.481 s — 0.168 s of tail, no fade, no silence, -10 dB and then the file is simply over. Also the half/double-time case: tagged 70.00, analyses at 139.95.

tracks.path: ~/Music/_Serato_/Imported/Serato Demo Tracks/05 - Hip Hop Track Serato Hip Hop Starter Pack.mp3
tracks.title: Hip Hop Track 05
tracks.note: Degenerate-case partner for 7004: identical BPM and identical key, the easiest mix that exists, so a beat-match failure here is a real bug rather than a tolerance issue. Fades out over ~3 s, the contrast to 7004's hard stop.
